rows.speaker: بعض الملحدين
rows.claim: Some objected that graciously recounting a gift is improper self-praise and unbecoming of the generous.
rows.anchor: طعن بعض الملحدين فقال كيف يحسن الامتنان بالإنعام وهل يكون هذا من فعل الكرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recounting a gift is blameworthy only to humiliate or hurt its recipient; reminding them to give thanks and seek further blessing is excellent, as a generous giver explains gifts so the recipient asks for needs.
rows.anchor: إن المن إنما يقبح من المنعم إذا أراد به الغض من المنعم عليه والأذى له

rows.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
rows.claim: Do not seize the orphan's property and deprive him of his right because he is weak.
rows.anchor: لا تقهره على ماله فتذهب بحقه لضعفه كما كانت تفعل العرب

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Alternatively, do not despise the orphan, since the Prophet himself had been an orphan.
rows.anchor: لا تحتقر اليتيم فقد كنت يتيما عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet treated orphans kindly and urged others to care for them.
rows.anchor: وكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يحسن إلى اليتامى ويبرهم ويوصي بهم

rows.speaker: أبو أوفى
rows.claim: An orphan boy asked the Prophet for food for himself, his orphan sister, and widowed mother; the Prophet sent 21 dates, seven for each, and Muadh comforted him. The Prophet praised Muadh and promised a good deed, erased sin, and a raised rank for every hair touched while properly caring for an orphan.
rows.anchor: عن أبي أوفى قال كنا جلوسا عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فأتاه غلام فقال غلام يتيم وأخت لي يتيمة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: The Prophet said that whoever strokes an orphan's head receives light on Judgment Day for every hair his hand passes over.
rows.anchor: من مسح على رأس يتيم كان له بكل شعرة تمر على يده نور يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet likened himself and a God-fearing caretaker of an orphan to the index and middle fingers together in Paradise.
rows.anchor: أنا وكافل اليتيم كهاتين في الجنة إذا اتقى الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب عن النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet said an orphan's crying shakes the Throne; God asks who made him cry and promises to please whoever soothes him on Judgment Day. Umar used to stroke orphans' heads and give them something.
rows.anchor: إن اليتيم إذا بكى اهتز لبكائه عرش الرحمن فيقول الله لملائكته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not rebuke or turn away a petitioner who asks you; having known poverty, either feed the petitioner or refuse gently.
rows.anchor: لا تنهر السائل ولا ترده إذا أتاك يسألك فقد كنت فقيرا فإما أن تطعمه

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك عن النبي
rows.claim: A petitioner arriving on horseback with hands outstretched is owed a right, even if only half a date is given.
rows.anchor: إذا أتاك سائل على فرس باسط كفيه فقد وجب له الحق ولو بشق تمرة

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: As God gave and showed mercy to you when you were needy, give to your petitioner and show mercy.
rows.anchor: يريد كما أعطاك الله ورحمك وأنت عائل فاعط سائلك وارحمه

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: The command addresses all morally responsible people, even though its immediate addressee is the Prophet.
rows.anchor: المراد بها جميع المكلفين وإن كان الخطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: The petitioner may be someone seeking knowledge; teach him the religious laws as God taught you when you did not know them, continuing the preceding reference to guidance.
rows.anchor: المراد بالسائل طلب العلم وهو متصل بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speak of God's gift, remember it, and make it known.
rows.anchor: معناه اذكر نعمة الله وأظهرها وحدث بها

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report says that whoever fails to thank people has not thanked God, and that mentioning God's gift is gratitude whereas concealing it is disbelief.
rows.anchor: من لم يشكر الناس لم يشكر الله ومن لم يشكر القليل لم يشكر الكثير

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: The blessing is the Quran, the greatest gift given to the Prophet, which he was commanded to recite.
rows.anchor: وكان القرآن أعظم ما أنعم الله عليه به فأمره أن يقرأه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The blessing is prophethood; al-Zajjaj selects this view and says the Prophet should convey his mission and speak of the prophethood God granted him, the greatest blessing.
rows.anchor: بالنبوة التي أعطاك ربك عن مجاهد واختاره الزجاج قال أي بلغ ما أرسلت به

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: Recount what God gave, favored, provided, bestowed, and guided you to.
rows.anchor: فحدث بما أعطاك الله وفضلك ورزقك وأحسن إليك وهداك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise that the Hereafter is better connects to the preceding reassurance of God's love and gifts: revelation and love endure, and the Prophet's future rank exceeds today's gifts; the connection from finding him needy to recounting favors joins gifts to their Giver and promises future favor as in the past.
rows.anchor: إثباتا لمحبته سبحانه إياه وإنعامه عليه فاتصل هذا أيضا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lexically, expansion opens something by removing what obstructs understanding; the root means widening. Joy is described as breadth of heart and distress as constriction because each produces that condition.
rows.anchor: الشرح فتح الشيء بإذهاب ما يصد عن إدراكه وأصل الشرح التوسعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wizr means a burden; vizier derives from bearing the ruler's burdens, and sins are called burdens for their great punishment.
rows.anchor: الوزر الثقل في اللغة ومنه اشتق اسم الوزير لتحمله أثقال الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anqad are loads that make what bears them creak; naqḍ and demolition are equivalent, and a camel is described as weighed down by travel.
rows.anchor: والأنقاض الأثقال التي كان ينتقض بها ما حمل عليه والنقض والهدم واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasb means fatigue; worry makes someone tired and afflicted.
rows.anchor: والنصب التعب وأنصبه الهم فهو منصب

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An anonymous poet uses mansab to describe a consuming worry and fatigue.
rows.anchor: تعناك هم من أميمة منصب

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nabigha's line uses nasib for a burdensome, tiring worry.
rows.anchor: كليني لهم يا أميمة ناصب

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: In a report, the Prophet recalls asking why earlier prophets had special signs; God reminded him of being sheltered as an orphan, guided, and given an expanded chest and removed burden.
rows.anchor: لقد سألت ربي مسألة وددت أني لم أساله قلت أي رب إنه قد كان أنبياء قبلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God opened the Prophet's chest and widened his heart through prophethood and knowledge, enabling him to deliver the message, endure harm, and remain settled in faith; God filled him with knowledge and wisdom, taught him Quran and Islamic law, and granted patience.
rows.anchor: ألم نفتح لك صدرك ونوسع قلبك بالنبوة والعلم حتى قمت بإداء الرسالة

rows.speaker: البلخي
rows.claim: The Prophet's chest had been constricted by hostility from jinn and humans; signs from God expanded it to bear his duties.
rows.anchor: كان قد ضاق صدره بمعاداة الجن والإنس إياه ومناصبتهم له

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Alternatively, God expanded the Prophet's chest by removing distractions that obstruct recognition of truth.
rows.anchor: معناه ألم نشرح صدرك بإذهاب الشواغل التي تصد عن إدراك الحق

rows.speaker: رسول الله عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: The Prophet says the sign of an expanded chest is turning away from the delusive world, returning to the eternal abode, and preparing for death before it arrives.
rows.anchor: نعم التجافي عن دار الغرور والإنابة إلى دار الخلود والإعداد للموت قبل نزول الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The confirming question means God had in fact expanded the Prophet's chest, as the coordinated statement that He removed his burden confirms.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الاستفهام في الآية التقرير أي قد فعلنا ذلك ويدل عليه قوله في العطف عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God lifted the Prophet's burden.
rows.anchor: أي وحططنا عنك وزرك

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: The burden had weighed on the Prophet so heavily that, had it been a physical load, one would hear his back creak.
rows.anchor: أي أثقله حتى سمع له نقيض أي صوت عن الزجاج

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة وعبد العزيز بن يحيى
rows.claim: The burden means the difficult obligations of prophethood, which God made easy to carry.
rows.anchor: تخفيف أعباء النبوة التي تثقل الظهر من القيام بأمرها

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: The burden means worries caused by the unbelievers' abuse, represented as a heavy load.
rows.anchor: وأزلنا عنك همومك التي أثقلتك من أذى الكفار فشبه الهموم بالحمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that God protected the Prophet from bearing sin; since removing a burden means leaving no weight, protection is an even fuller removal.
rows.anchor: وعصمناك عن احتمال الوزر فإن المقصود من الوضع أن لا يكون عليه ثقل

rows.speaker: المرتضى
rows.claim: Since sins are called burdens because they weigh down and distress their bearer, the burden here may instead be the Prophet's grief over his people's idolatry and his and his followers' oppression; God's later strengthening of Islam removed that grief. This fits the following easing of grief better than removing sin.
rows.anchor: فلا يمتنع أن يكون الوزر في الآية إنما أراد به غمه صلى الله عليه وسلم بما كان عليه قومه من الشرك

rows.speaker: المرتضى
rows.claim: An objection says the surah is Meccan and predates Islam's triumph; the answer is that God's promise of victory already lifted the Prophet's grief, and a past-tense verb can describe the future.
rows.anchor: إن السورة مكية نزلت قبل أن يعلي الله كلمة الإسلام فلا وجه لقولكم

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة والضحاك ومقاتل والكلبي
rows.claim: One interpretation is: after finishing the prescribed prayer, labor in supplication to God and ask Him, and He will give; the same interpretation is transmitted from Abu Jaafar and Abu Abdullah.
rows.anchor: من الصلاة المكتوبة فانصب إلى ربك في الدعاء وارغب إليه في المسألة يعطك عن مجاهد وقتادة والضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to strive derives from fatigue and means not to occupy oneself with rest.
rows.anchor: ومعنى انصب من النصب وهو التعب أي لا تشتغل بالراحة

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: After completing the obligations, make supplication after the tashahhud with all one's needs.
rows.anchor: إذا فرغت من الفرائض فادع بعد التشهد بكل حاجتك

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: The verse means supplication after prayer while sitting.
rows.anchor: هو الدعاء في دبر الصلاة وأنت جالس

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: After the obligatory prayers, devote oneself to standing in night prayer.
rows.anchor: فإذا فرغت من الفرائض فانصب في قيام الليل عن ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: مجاهد والجبائي
rows.claim: Alternatively, after finishing worldly affairs, devote effort to worship and prayer.
rows.anchor: فإذا فرغت من دنياك فانصب في عبادة ربك وصل عن مجاهد والجبائي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: After the obligations, strive in the good works God has encouraged and pray.
rows.anchor: فإذا فرغت من الفرائض فانصب فيما رغبك الله فيه من الأعمال وصل عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الحسن وابن زيد
rows.claim: When finished with fighting enemies, devote oneself to worship of God.
rows.anchor: إذا فرغت من جهاد أعدائك فانصب بالعبادة لله عن الحسن وابن زيد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation is to finish fighting the enemy and then struggle against one's own soul.
rows.anchor: فإذا فرغت من جهاد الأعداء فانصب بجهاد نفسك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation is to finish delivering the message and then strive to seek intercession.
rows.anchor: من أداء الرسالة فانصب لطلب الشفاعة

rows.speaker: علي بن طلحة
rows.claim: After noting the many interpretations, he transmits the saying that one should make health and free time an exertion in worship.
rows.anchor: إذا صححت فاجعل صحتك وفراغك نصبا في العبادة

rows.speaker: شريح
rows.claim: Seeing two men wrestling, Shurayh said that was not the task of a person with free time; the verse directs one to raise needs to God rather than any creature.
rows.anchor: مر برجلين يصطرعان فقال ليس بهذا أمر الفارغ إنما قال الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Desire God while fearing Hell and hoping for Paradise.
rows.anchor: يريد تضرع إليه راهبا من النار وراغبا إلى الجنة

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: When he finished reciting this surah, the Prophet would answer that indeed he is among those who bear witness to this.
rows.anchor: بلى وأنا على ذلك من الشاهدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse follows the mention of religion and recompense as a warning that resurrection must bring justice: a wise judge who commands and prohibits and leaves wrongdoers and victims unreconciled must repay them if justice did not occur in this world.
rows.anchor: بما قبله من ذكر الدين والجزاء على سبيل التنبيه على الإعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alaq is the plural of a coagulated piece of blood that clings while moist and is no longer called that once dry; al-alaq also names a black leech that clings to a limb and sucks blood.
rows.anchor: العلق جمع علقة وهي القطعة الجامدة من الدم التي تعلق لرطوبتها بما تمر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ruj'a and al-marjiʿ both mean return.
rows.anchor: والرجعى الرجوع والمرجع واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Safʿ means a forceful grasp and pull; the sun or fire can also disfigure and blacken someone's face, as in a report about people scorched by fire.
rows.anchor: السفع الجذب الشديد يقال سفعت بالشيء إذا قبضت عليه وجذبته جذبا شديدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forehead lock is hair at the front of the head, so named for being attached to it; the root denotes joining.
rows.anchor: والناصية شعر مقدم الرأس سميت بذلك لأنها متصلة بالرأس

rows.speaker: الراجز
rows.claim: An anonymous rajaz poet uses tanasiha in a line as evidence for the root meaning of joining.
rows.anchor: سميت بذلك لأنها متصلة بالرأس من قولهم ناصى يناصي مناصاة إذا وصل قال الراجز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-nadi originally means the gathering place of the council's people, then came to mean any gathering.
rows.anchor: النادي مجلس أهل النادي ثم كثر فسمي كل مجلس ناديا

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة والكسائي والأخفش
rows.claim: The singular of zabaniya is given variously as zabina, zabna, or zabin; the term derives from pushing, as a camel pushes its milker away with its leg.
rows.anchor: وواحد الزبانية زبينة عن أبي عبيدة وزبنى عن الكسائي وزابن عن الأخفش

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses the verb zabana to mean that war would push or jolt someone.
rows.anchor: ومستعجب مما يرى من أناتنا ولو زبنته الحرب لم يترمرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning creation of the human after the general creation is specification after generality, like naming belief in the afterlife after unseen belief; Labid's line shows that blame is broader than calling someone slow.
rows.anchor: بعد قوله خلق خصوص بعد عموم فهو مثل قوله

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labid's line illustrates that accusation of slowness is a subset of reproach, so the latter is more general.
rows.anchor: أو أن يلوم بحاجة لوامها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, the hidden subject of ra'ahu returns to the hidden subject of yatgha, and its object pronoun also refers to that subject; this is allowed with verbs of knowing because their predicate is the subject itself, unlike ordinary verbs that need nafsi.
rows.anchor: الضمير المستكن في رآه عائد إلى الضمير المستكن في يطغى والهاء في رآه عائد إلى الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ra'ahu istaghna is a second object of ra'ahu, with the implied sense that he sees himself self-sufficient.
rows.anchor: التقدير لأن رآه مستغنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasiyah is an apposition explaining the forehead lock as its owner's lying, erring head, like saying a person's day fasts and night stands in prayer.
rows.anchor: بناصية صاحبها كاذب خاطىء يقال فلان نهاره صائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 'let him call his gathering', people is elided after gathering: the intended meaning is the people of his council.
rows.anchor: أي أهل ناديه فحذف المضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic n in lansasfaʿan is light; Basrans prefer writing it with alif to reflect pausal form, while Kufans prefer n because it is truly a n.
rows.anchor: نون التأكيد الخفيفة والاختيار عند البصريين أن تكتب بالألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening command tells the Prophet to recite in God's name and invoke Him by His beautiful names; honoring the name honors the named one, which only someone who knows God and believes in worship can truly do.
rows.anchor: هذا أمر من الله سبحانه لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يقرأ باسم ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prefixed bi is extra in the command, which can be read as 'recite your Lord's name'; the source links the invocation of God or al-Rahman to His beautiful names.
rows.anchor: فالباء هنا زائدة والتقدير اقرأ باسم ربك

rows.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes say this surah was the first Quran revelation; Gabriel first came to the Prophet on Hira and taught him its first five verses.
rows.anchor: وأكثر المفسرين على أن هذه السورة أول ما نزل من القرآن وأول يوم نزل جبرائيل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative says the first revelation was 'O you who are wrapped up'.
rows.anchor: أول ما نزل من القرآن قوله

rows.speaker: أبو ميسرة عمرو بن شرحبيل
rows.claim: An alternative report says the Opening was the first surah revealed: the Prophet told Khadija he heard a call in solitude; she reassured him, took him to Waraqa, who identified him as a prophet like Moses and foretold his mission and struggle. After Waraqa died, the Prophet said he saw him in Paradise in silk for believing him.
rows.anchor: رواه الحاكم أبو عبد الله الحافظ بإسناده عن أبي ميسرة عمرو بن شرحبيل أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لخديجة

rows.speaker: ورقة بن نوفل
rows.claim: Waraqa tells Khadija and the Prophet that Gabriel brings the revelation, that the Prophet is sent, and that he will be commanded to struggle; Waraqa promises to support him if alive.
rows.anchor: فلما خلا ناداه يا محمد قل له ذلك فقال له أبشر

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: After Waraqa's death, the Prophet said he saw the priest in Paradise wearing silk because he believed and affirmed him.
rows.anchor: لقد رأيت القس في الجنة عليه ثياب الحرير لأنه آمن بي وصدقني

rows.speaker: ورقة بن نوفل
rows.claim: Waraqa's poem calls Ahmad a messenger and says Gabriel and Michael bring revelation from God that expands the chest, sorting people between Paradise and Hell.
rows.anchor: فإن يك حقا يا خديجة فاعلمي حديثك إيانا فأحمد مرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created all creatures according to wisdom and power, then singles out the human for honor among animals; humankind comes from coagulated blood after the sperm. The source prefers this over the view that Adam was made from hand-clinging clay. The lowly origin's development into balanced humanity parallels the Prophet's transformation from ignorance to prophethood.
rows.anchor: أراد به جنس بني آدم أي خلقتهم من دم جامد بعد النطفة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A competing reading says the verse means Adam was made from clay that clings to the hand; the author says the account of humankind's origin is sounder.
rows.anchor: معناه خلق آدم من طين يعلق باليد والأول أصح

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: The repeated command is not redundant: the first tells him to recite for himself and the second to recite for conveying the message.
rows.anchor: أمره في الأول بالقراءة لنفسه وفي الثاني بالقراءة للتبليغ وليس بتكرار عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord is the most generous, whose generosity no other generous giver can match: every blessing comes from Him by creation or by providing its means.
rows.anchor: الأعظم كرما فلا يبلغه كرم كريم لأنه يعطي من النعم ما لا يقدر على مثله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the command is to convey the message to the people; the Most Generous rewards the Prophet, strengthens him, and helps him retain the Quran.
rows.anchor: بلغ قومك وربك الأكرم الذي يثيبك على عملك بما يقتضيه كرمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God taught the scribe to write, taught people expression through the pen, or taught writing by means of the pen; writing benefits religion and worldly life.
rows.anchor: علم الكاتب أن يكتب بالقلم أو علم الإنسان البيان بالقلم أو علم الكتابة بالقلم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The pen is a tremendous blessing from God: without it religion would not stand and life would not improve.
rows.anchor: القلم نعمة من الله عظيمة لولاه لم يقم دين ولم يصلح عيش

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: An unattributed poem describes the pen's ink as venomous serpents' saliva and the gathered honey of hands, praising its striking material effect.
rows.anchor: لعاب الأفاعي القاتلات لعابه وأري الجنى اشتارته أيد عواسل

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: A report says Adam was the first to write.
rows.anchor: وقيل أراد سبحانه آدم لأنه أول من كتب عن كعب

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: A report says Idris was the first to write.
rows.anchor: أول من كتب إدريس عن الضحاك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The verse may refer to every prophet who wrote with a pen, since God alone taught each of them to write.
rows.anchor: أراد كل نبي كتب بالقلم لأنه ما علمه إلا بتعليم الله إياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God taught people guidance, expression, religion, laws, and rulings; human knowledge comes through intuition, rational evidence, or teaching by angels and messengers, so all knowledge is attributable to Him. This indicates that God is knowing, since knowledge comes only from a knower.
rows.anchor: من أنواع الهدى والبيان وأمور الدين والشرائع والأحكام فجميع ما يعلمه الإنسان من جهته سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla here means truly; a human exceeds bounds, grows proud against his Lord, and transgresses his proper limit.
rows.anchor: أي يتجاوز حد ويستكبر على ربه ويعدو طوره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person transgresses because he sees himself independent of God through kin, wealth, or strength; it is the belief in self-sufficiency, not actual wealth, that produces tyranny.
rows.anchor: لأن رآه نفسه مستغنية عن ربه بعشيرته وأمواله وقوته

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: When a man gained wealth, he expanded his clothes, mount, food, and drink; that was his transgression.
rows.anchor: كان إذا أصاب مالا زاد في ثيابه ومركبه وطعامه وشرابه فذلك طغيانه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One report says the passage from here to the end of the surah was revealed concerning Abu Jahl.
rows.anchor: إنها نزلت في أبي جهل بن هشام من هنا إلى آخر السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone returns to God; therefore the wealthy tyrant should not transgress, since God can destroy and punish him at his return.
rows.anchor: إلى الله مرجع كل أحد أي فهذا الطاغي كيف يطغى بماله ويعصي ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question draws the Prophet's attention to what God will do to someone who prevents him from praying; the omitted consequence is understood from the context.
rows.anchor: هذا تقرير للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وإعلام له بما يفعله بمن ينهاه عن الصلاة

rows.speaker: أبو جهل
rows.claim: Abu Jahl threatened to trample Muhammad's neck if he saw him praying; when he approached, he recoiled, seeing a trench of fire, terror, and wings, and the Prophet said angels would tear him limb from limb. Muslim records the report in his Sahih.
rows.anchor: أن أبا جهل قال هل يعفر محمد وجهه بين أظهركم قالوا نعم قال فبالذي يحلف به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks what becomes of one who forbids prayer and what punishment he deserves; it applies generally to anyone forbidding prayer or good, and expresses amazement.
rows.anchor: والآية عامة في كل من ينهى عن الصلاة والخير

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: On a festival, Ali saw people praying before the imam; when asked to prohibit it, he refused to forbid a worshipper and instead recalled the Prophet's practice.
rows.anchor: وروي عن علي أنه خرج في يوم عيد فرأى ناسا يصلون فقال يا أيها الناس قد شهدنا نبي الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating 'Have you seen?' intensifies the exclamation about the forbidden worshipper.
rows.anchor: ومعنى أرأيت ها هنا تعجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one being forbidden is the rightly guided servant, Muhammad, or the one commanding piety through sincerity, monotheism, and fear of God; the implied question is what becomes of his forbidding opponent.
rows.anchor: يعني العبد المنهي وهو محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who denies and turns away is Abu Jahl, rejecting faith and refusing to listen.
rows.anchor: عن الإيمان وأعرض عن قبوله والإصغاء إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sees his actions and knows what he does; the implied question asks what punishment this behavior deserves. The verse also signals that one must obey and leave sin.
rows.anchor: ما يفعله ويعلم ما يصنعه والتقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternate syntactic arrangement contrasts the worshipper, who is guided and commands piety, with the denier who turns away, then warns that God sees the denier's reprehensible act and will hold him to account.
rows.anchor: أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى وهو على الهدى آمر بالتقوى والناهي كاذب مكذب متول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla means he does not know; if Abu Jahl does not stop denying Muhammad and harming him, God will drag him by his forelock toward the fire.
rows.anchor: يعني إن لم يمتنع أبو جهل عن تكذيب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وإيذائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dragging by the forelock humiliates and disgraces him, as in the verse about taking sinners by their forelocks and feet; alternatively, fire burns and blackens his face.
rows.anchor: ومعناه لنذلنه ونقيمنه مقام الأذلة ففي الأخذ بالناصية إهانة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: When Abu Jahl confronted the Prophet and boasted that no one had a larger council, the Prophet rebuked him; the passage about calling his gathering was revealed.
rows.anchor: لما أتى أبو جهل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم انتهره رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forehead lock is described as lying and erring to mean that its owner lies in speech and errs in actions.
rows.anchor: وصفها بالكذب والخطأ بمعنى أن صاحبها كاذب في أقواله خاطىء في أفعاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat means Abu Jahl may call his council's people and clan to help him when God's punishment comes; nadi can also mean an open courtyard.
rows.anchor: أي أهل مجلسه يعني عشيرته فليستنصر بهم إذا حل عقاب الله به والنادي الفناء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: If Abu Jahl had called his council, the keepers of Hell would have seized him immediately in plain sight.
rows.anchor: لو دعا ناديه لأخذته زبانية النار من ساعته معاينة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verse announces that God will summon the angels whether Abu Jahl calls his council or not; his death at Badr confirmed it.
rows.anchor: إخبار بأنه يدعو إليه الزبانية دعا ناديه أم لم يدع وصدق سبحانه ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zabaniya are the harsh, strong angels assigned to Hell.
rows.anchor: يعني الملائكة الموكلين بالنار وهم الملائكة الغلاظ الشداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla rejects Abu Jahl's position: do not obey his ban on prayer; prostrate to God and draw near to His reward.
rows.anchor: ليس الأمر على ما عليه أبو جهل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Drawing near means approaching God through obedience; the servant is closest to God while prostrating, or the command means pray to God.
rows.anchor: اسجد يا محمد للتقرب منه فإن أقرب ما يكون

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود عن النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet said that a servant is closest to God while prostrating.
rows.anchor: أقرب ما يكون العبد من الله إذا كان ساجدا

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن سنان عن أبي عبد الله
rows.claim: Prostration at the end of this surah is obligatory; the four obligatory recitation prostrations are in al-Sajda, Fussilat, al-Najm, and this surah, while all others are recommended.
rows.anchor: وما عداها في جميع القرآن مسنون وليس بمفروض

rows.speaker: الكسائي وخلف
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read matlaʿ with a kasra; the remaining canonical readers use a fatha.
rows.anchor: قرأ الكسائي وخلف مطلع بكسر اللام والباقون بفتح اللام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة والكلبي
rows.claim: A rare reading has min kulli imriʾ, 'from every person'.
rows.anchor: وفي الشواذ قراءة ابن عباس وعكرمة والكلبي من كل امرء

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Matlaʿ is a verbal noun meaning the time of sunrise, as in the time a caravan arrives or a star sets; fatha fits the usual noun pattern, while kasra is supported by other verbal nouns.
rows.anchor: مطلع هنا مصدر بدلالة أن المعنى سلام هي حتى وقت طلوعه

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni says Abu Hatim rejected the reading min kulli imriʾ, while Ibn Abbas reportedly explained the words as the angels descending from every commander; Ibn Jinni instead joins min kulli amr to the prior clause as a complete phrase.
rows.anchor: أنكر أبو حاتم هذه القراءة على أنه حكي عن ابن عباس أنه قال

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub reads the night as peace from every affair and every person; this requires سلام to function as an active participle so its complement may precede it.
rows.anchor: وقال قطرب معناه هي سلام من كل أمر وأمرىء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In response to the objection about word order, سلام here is used like the active participle safe or protected, meaning the night is safe from every affair.
rows.anchor: سلاما في الأصل كعمري مصدر فأما هنا فإنه موضوع موضع اسم الفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadr can mean a thing's measure or equality without increase or decrease; God's determining a matter means setting it according to wisdom.
rows.anchor: القدر كون الشيء مساويا لغيره من غير زيادة ولا نقصان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A legal month runs between two new moons and has 29 or 30 days if lunar; a non-lunar month has 30.
rows.anchor: والشهر في الشرع عبارة عما بين هلالين من الأيام وإنما سمي شهرا لاشتهاره بالهلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison means better than a thousand months without a Night of Decree, with the adjective omitted.
rows.anchor: تقديره خير من ألف شهر لا ليلة قدر فيه فحذف الصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In سلام هي, هي is the subject and سلام its advanced predicate, understood as an active participle; treating it as an infinitive breaks the attachment of hatta to its clause.
rows.anchor: هي مبتدأ وسلام خبر مقدم عليه وهو بمعنى الفاعل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: God sent the entire Quran from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven on the Night of Decree, then Gabriel revealed it to Muhammad in portions over 23 years.
rows.anchor: أنزل الله القرآن جملة واحدة من اللوح المحفوظ إلى السماء الدنيا في ليلة القدر

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: The verse means God began revealing the Quran on the Night of Decree.
rows.anchor: معناه أنا ابتدأنا إنزاله في ليلة القدر

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: The Quran was sent from the Preserved Tablet to the angelic scribes in the lowest heaven; each Night of Decree they received the year's revelation in proportion to what Gabriel would deliver through the year.
rows.anchor: أنزله من اللوح المحفوظ إلى السفرة وهم الكتبة من الملائكة في السماء الدنيا

rows.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
rows.claim: The night is named for decree because God decides that year's events in it; it is the blessed night of 44:3, when He sends down good, blessing, and forgiveness.
rows.anchor: فقيل سميت ليلة القدر لأنها الليلة التي يحكم الله فيها ويقضي بما يكون في السنة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن أبي الضحى
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reportedly said destinies were decided on mid-Sha'ban and handed to those responsible for them on the Night of Decree.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو الضحى عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقضي القضايا في ليلة النصف من شعبان

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: The name may mean a night of rank, distinction, and high standing.
rows.anchor: ليلة القدر أي ليلة الشرف والخطر وعظم الشأن من قولهم رجل له قدر

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
rows.claim: Al-Warraq explains that someone of no standing gains distinction by worshipping on it; another explanation is that its acts of worship carry immense merit and reward.
rows.anchor: لأن من لم يكن ذا قدر إذا أحياها صار ذا قدر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: It is a night of honor because a weighty Book came to an honored Messenger for an honored community through an honored angel.
rows.anchor: سميت ليلة القدر لأنه أنزل فيها كتاب ذو قدر إلى رسول ذي قدر لأجل أمة ذات قدر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: It may be called the Night of Decree because God decreed the Quran's revelation on it.
rows.anchor: هي ليلة التقدير لأن الله تعالى قدر فيها إنزال القرآن

rows.speaker: الخليل بن أحمد
rows.claim: The night may be named because the earth becomes crowded by angels, using the expression 'He constricted his provision' as an example.
rows.anchor: سميت بذلك لأن الأرض تضيق فيها بالملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poet uses sawaʾ to mean equal; the syntax implies asking whether the speaker's guarantors are equal in fidelity, since a verbal noun cannot have its complement precede it.
rows.anchor: سواء بمعنى مستو والتقدير فهل كفلائي مستوون في الوفاء

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet's line supplies the example with sawaʾ in a question about equal fidelity.
rows.anchor: فهلا سعيتم سعي عصبة مازن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hatta may attach to the angels' descent, but هي cannot be the subject with حتى as an indefinite predicate; matlaʿ is governed by حتى with the sense 'until'.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون هي مبتدأ وتكون حتى نكرة في موضع الخبر

rows.speaker: أبو ذر عن النبي
rows.claim: Abu Dharr asked whether the Night of Decree existed only for earlier prophets and was lifted after they died; the Prophet answered that it continues until the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: جاءت الرواية عن أبي ذر أنه قال قلت يا رسول الله ليلة القدر هي شيء تكون على عهد الأنبياء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view places the night somewhere among all the year's nights; Abu Hanifa holds that a divorce made conditional on it does not take effect until a year has passed.
rows.anchor: إنها في ليالي السنة كلها ومن علق طلاق امرأته على ليلة القدر

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: In one report, Ibn Masud says someone who prays through the whole year will find the night; Ibn Umar says he knew it was in Ramadan but urged people not to rely on one night.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض الروايات عن ابن مسعود أنه قال من يقم الحول كله يصبها

rows.speaker: جمهور العلماء
rows.claim: The majority hold that the Night of Decree occurs every year in Ramadan; its exact night is disputed.
rows.anchor: وجمهور العلماء على أنها في شهر رمضان في كل سنة ثم اختلفوا في أي ليلة هي منه

rows.speaker: ابن زيد العقيلي
rows.claim: One view places it on Ramadan's first night.
rows.anchor: فقيل هي أول ليلة منه عن ابن زيد العقيلي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Another view places it on Ramadan 17 and calls it the Night of Criterion, whose morning saw the two armies meet.
rows.anchor: هي ليلة سبع عشرة منه عن الحسن وروي أنها ليلة الفرقان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soundest position is that it falls in Ramadan's final ten nights, which is the Shafi'i school; a Prophetic report commands seeking it then.
rows.anchor: والصحيح أنها في العشر الآواخر من شهر رمضان وهو مذهب الشافعي

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali reports that in the last ten nights the Prophet woke his family, worked hard, and urged them to do so.
rows.anchor: وعن علي ع أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يوقظ أهله في العشر الأواخر

rows.speaker: أبو بصير عن أبي عبد الله
rows.claim: When the last ten nights began, the Prophet tightened his belt, avoided intimacy, stayed awake through the night, and devoted himself to worship.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو بصير عن أبي عبد الله ع قال كان رسول إذا دخل العشر الأواخر شد المئزر

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري عن النبي
rows.claim: Abu Said identifies the 21st: the Prophet dreamed he prostrated in water and mud, told people to seek the night in the last ten and on odd nights, and awoke on the 21st with mud on his face.
rows.anchor: رأيت هذه الليلة ثم أنسيتها ورأيتني أسجد في ماء وطين

rows.speaker: رسول الله عن ابن عمر
rows.claim: After a man dreamed that the Night of Decree was the seventh night remaining, the Prophet said their visions converged on the 23rd and urged anyone praying part of the month to pray then.
rows.anchor: جاء رجل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال يا رسول إني رأيت في النوم كأن ليلة القدر هي ليلة سابعة تبقى

rows.speaker: معمر
rows.claim: Ma'mar says Ayyub would bathe and apply perfume on Ramadan 23.
rows.anchor: كان أيوب يغتسل ليلة ثلاث وعشرين ويمس طيبا

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar asked the Companions which odd night they thought it fell on; most selected an odd night.
rows.anchor: وسأل عمر بن الخطاب أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال قد علمتم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reasons for the 23rd by God's repeated use of seven: seven heavens and earths, seven circuits and stones, seven stages of human creation, and seven categories of provision; Umar praises his insight and knowledge.
rows.anchor: فقلت رأيت الله أكثر ذكر السبع في القرآن فذكر السماوات سبعا والأرضين سبعا

rows.speaker: عبد الواحد بن المختار الأنصاري عن زرارة عن أبي جعفر
rows.claim: A report locates the Night of Decree on both the 21st and 23rd; when asked to choose one, the Imam says it is easy to act on both.
rows.anchor: سألت أبا جعفر ع عن ليلة القدر قال في ليلتين ليلة ثلاث وعشرين وإحدى وعشرين

rows.speaker: شهاب بن عبد ربه عن أبي عبد الله
rows.claim: One report identifies the 21st and 23rd nights.
rows.anchor: عن شهاب بن عبد ربه قال قلت لأبي عبد الله ع أخبرني بليلة القدر فقال ليلة إحدى وعشرين وليلة ثلاث وعشرين

rows.speaker: حسان بن أبي علي عن أبي عبد الله
rows.claim: Another report says to seek the Night of Decree on the 19th, 21st, and 23rd.
rows.anchor: عن حماد بن عثمان عن حسان بن أبي علي قال سألت أبا عبد الله ع عن ليلة القدر قال اطلبها في تسع عشرة

rows.speaker: أبو بصير عن أبي عبد الله
rows.claim: A report recommends the 21st and 23rd; if one cannot observe both, the Imam says two nights are easy, and if local moon reports differ, four nights are easy. The 23rd is called the Juhani night.
rows.anchor: هي ليلة إحدى وعشرين وثلاث وعشرين قال فإن لم أقو على كلتيهما فقال ما أيسر ليلتين

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: The Imam says pilgrims' delegations, lifespans, calamities, and provisions are determined on the Night of Decree until the next year; seek it on the 21st or 23rd, pray 100 rakas, stay up, and bathe. If unable to stand, pray seated or in bed; rest early if needed. Ramadan's heavenly gates open, devils are chained, and believers' deeds accepted; the month was called al-Marzūq in the Prophet's time.
rows.anchor: وفد الحاج يكتب في ليلة القدر والمنايا والبلايا والأرزاق ما يكون إلى مثلها في قابل

rows.speaker: أحد الإمامين عن زرارة
rows.claim: A report recommends ritual washing on Ramadan nights 19, 21, and 23, and calls the 23rd the Juhani night.
rows.anchor: سألته عن الليالي التي يستحب فيها الغسل في شهر رمضان فقال ليلة تسع عشرة وليلة إحدى وعشرين وليلة ثلاث وعشرين

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب وعائشة
rows.claim: One view places the night on the 27th; Ibn Abbas and Ibn Umar report the Prophet urging people to seek it then.
rows.anchor: إنها ليلة سبع وعشرين عن أبي بن كعب وعائشة

rows.speaker: زر بن حبيش عن أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy says the Prophet's sign for the 27th was that the next morning's sun would rise like a basin with no rays.
rows.anchor: قلت لأبي يا أبا المنذر من أين علمت أنها ليلة سبع وعشرين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some infer the 27th by dividing the surah's words across Ramadan's nights and taking its reference there.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم إن الله قسم كلمات السورة على ليالي شهر رمضان فلما بلغ السابعة والعشرين

rows.speaker: أبو بكرة عن النبي
rows.claim: A report says to seek it in the last ten on a night with nine, seven, five, or three remaining, or on the final night.
rows.anchor: التمسوها في العشر الأواخر في تسع بقين أو سبع بقين أو خمس بقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God concealed the night so people would strive through all Ramadan nights, just as He concealed the middle prayer, greatest name, and Friday's hour of answered prayer.
rows.anchor: والفائدة في إخفاء هذه الليلة أن يجتهد الناس في العبادة ويحيوا جميع ليالي شهر رمضان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن النبي
rows.claim: On the Night of Decree, angels from the lote tree, including Gabriel, descend with banners over the Prophet's grave, Jerusalem, the Sacred Mosque, and Sinai, greeting every believer except persistent wine drinkers, pork eaters, and those doused in saffron.
rows.anchor: روى ابن عباس عن النبي أنه قال إذا كان ليلة القدر تنزل الملائكة الذين هم سكان سدرة المنتهى

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Whoever stands in prayer on the Night of Decree in faith and seeking reward is forgiven for prior sins.
rows.anchor: من قام ليلة القدر إيمانا واحتسابا غفر له ما تقدم من ذنبه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report says Satan stays away until dawn and cannot cause insanity, illness, corruption, or let a sorcerer's magic take effect on anyone that night.
rows.anchor: إن الشيطان لا يخرج في هذه الليلة حتى يضيء فجرها ولا يستطيع فيها على أحد بخبل أو داء

rows.speaker: رسول الله عن عبد الله بن أنيس الجهني
rows.claim: The source begins a report in which the Prophet specifies the 23rd for a man who lived far from Medina; Abu Jaafar identifies him as Abdullah ibn Anis al-Ansari.
rows.anchor: إن منزلي نأى عن المدينة فمرني بليلة أدخل فيها فأمره بليلة ثلاث وعشرين

rows.speaker: الحسن عن النبي
rows.claim: The Night of Decree is mild, neither hot nor cold, and the morning sun rises without rays.
rows.anchor: إنها ليلة سمحة لا حارة ولا باردة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question magnifies the night’s status and sacredness and urges the Prophet to worship in it.
rows.anchor: وما أدراك يا محمد ما خطر ليلة القدر وما حرمتها وهذا حث على العبادة فيها

rows.speaker: مقاتل وقتادة
rows.claim: Standing and worshipping on the Night of Decree is better than a thousand months of worship and fasting without it, because times are superior according to the good they contain.
rows.anchor: قيام ليلة القدر والعمل فيها خير من قيام ألف شهر ليس فيه ليلة القدر وصيامه عن مقاتل وقتادة

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet was amazed at an Israelite who bore arms for God's cause for a thousand months and wished his community could do likewise; God granted this night as a gift to the Prophet and his community every Ramadan until the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: رجل من بني إسرائيل أنه حمل السلاح على عاتقه في سبيل الله تعالى ألف شهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Spirit is Gabriel, and the angels descend to earth to hear praise, Quran, and remembrance.
rows.anchor: أي في ليلة القدر إلى الأرض ليسمعوا الثناء على الله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the angels descend to greet Muslims at God's command or carry every decree to the lowest heaven for its inhabitants to know, as a kindness to them.
rows.anchor: ينزلون بكل أمر إلى السماء الدنيا حتى يعلم ذلك أهل السماء الدنيا

rows.speaker: كعب ومقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: The Spirit is a group of angels whom other angels cannot see; they descend from sunset to dawn.
rows.anchor: الروح طائفة من الملائكة لا تراهم الملائكة إلا تلك الليلة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The Spirit may be revelation, as in 42:52; thus angels descend with revelation concerning decreed good and benefits.
rows.anchor: الروح هو الوحي كما قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By God's permission means by His command, as in the verse about angels guarding by God's command; another interpretation is by His knowledge.
rows.anchor: أي بأمر ربهم كما قال وما نتنزل إلا بأمر ربك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Min kulli amr can mean every good and blessing, every command, or each provision and decree lasting through the next year's corresponding night; on the last reading the pause belongs after this phrase.
rows.anchor: أي بكل أمر من الخير والبركة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The night is peaceful until dawn, safe from evils, afflictions, and Satan's harms.
rows.anchor: أي هذه ليلة إلى آخرها سلامة من الشرور والبلايا وآفات الشيطان

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The night is free of evil arising or of a devil being able to act in it.
rows.anchor: يعني أن ليلة القدر سالمة عن أن يحدث فيها سوء

rows.speaker: عطاء والكلبي
rows.claim: Alternatively, angels convey God's greeting of peace to His obedient friends throughout the night.
rows.anchor: سلام على أولياء الله وأهل طاعته فكلما لقيهم الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parsing ends the clause at God's permission and begins min kulli amr سلام: every matter contains safety, benefit, good, and blessing; this lasts through the whole night until dawn.
rows.anchor: أي بكل أمر فيه سلامة ومنفعة وخير وبركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the interpretation of the Spirit as revelation, the angels descend with revelation carrying decreed good and benefits.
rows.anchor: تنزل الملائكة ومعهم الوحي بتقدير الخيرات والمنافع

rows.speaker: نافع وابن ذكوان
rows.claim: Nafi and Ibn Dhakwan pronounce al-bariyya with hamza; the other readers omit it.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن ذكوان البريئة مهموزة والباقون بغير همزة

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Since the word derives from God's creating, its etymology would have hamza, but popular usage dropped it as in nabi, dhurriyya, and khabiya; retaining it restores an abandoned original, while dropping it is better-established usage and the hamza refutes derivation from dust.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي البريئة من برأ الله الخلق فالقياس فيه الهمز إلا أنه مما ترك همزه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Infikak means separation after strong attachment and is used mostly with negation, as in a line by Dhu al-Rumma about camels that only stop to kneel or be driven to a remote land.
rows.anchor: قلائص ما تنفك إلا مناخة على الخسف أو نرمي بها بلدا قفرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayyina is a clear proof distinguishing truth from falsehood; its root carries the sense of separation. The Prophet, fair testimony, and every proof are called bayyina.
rows.anchor: والبينة الحجة الظاهرة التي يتميز بها الحق من الباطل وأصلها من البينونة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qayyima means upright and consistent in what is correct. Hanif means inclined toward the truth; an alternative derives it from uprightness and calls a slanted foot hanif as a hopeful inversion.
rows.anchor: والقيمة المستمرة في جهة الصواب والحنيف المائل إلى الصواب والحق

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: In the syntax, 'a messenger from God' may be an apposition explaining the preceding proof, or al-Farra treats it as a new sentence with an implied 'he'.
rows.anchor: رسول من الله بدل من البينة قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To avoid annexing a noun to its own attribute, 'religion of the upright' has an implied 'religion of the upright community'. In the reward clause, entry into Eden is implied and 'remaining' describes the hidden subject of their reward.
rows.anchor: دين القيمة تقديره دين لملة القيمة لأنه إذا لم يقدر ذلك كان إضافة الشيء إلى صفته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse addresses Jews, Christians, and idol-worshipping polytheists from Arabs and others; munfakkin can mean separating or stopping from disbelief and worship of others, an interpretation attributed to Ibn Abbas through Ata and al-Kalbi.
rows.anchor: ومن المشركين الذين هم عبدة الأوثان من العرب وغيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future-tense phrase until the proof came refers to the past, as in the statement about what demons recited in 2:102.
rows.anchor: اللفظ لفظ الاستقبال ومعناه المضي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
rows.claim: The proof is Muhammad, who clarified their deviation and idolatry; the unbelievers did not stop until he came, showed their error, and called them to faith. 'A messenger from God' explains the proof.
rows.anchor: يريد محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم عن ابن عباس ومقاتل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, they could not leave unbelief until God's proof came and established the argument against them.
rows.anchor: لم يكونوا ليتركوا منفكين من حجج الله حتى تأتيهم البينة التي تقوم بها الحجة عليهم

rows.speaker: الحسن والجبائي
rows.claim: The purified pages are pure in heaven, touched only by purified angels, and Muhammad delivered them as the Quran, calling people to monotheism and faith.
rows.anchor: يعني مطهرة في السماء لا يمسها إلا الملائكة المطهرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scripture pages contain straight, just books without distortion that distinguish truth from falsehood.
rows.anchor: أي مستقيمة عادلة غير ذات عوج تبين الحق من الباطل

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Purified pages means the Quran, free of falsehood, lies, and slander; pages refers to their written contents, although the Prophet recited from memory rather than a book.
rows.anchor: عن الباطل والكذب والزور يريد القرآن عن قتادة

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Alternatively, the messenger is an angel reciting pages from the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: رسول من الملائكة يتلو صحفا من اللوح المحفوظ عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The Quran itself contains the upright books by encompassing earlier scriptures, as shown by its confirmation of what preceded it; whoever recites it recites those books.
rows.anchor: إن القرآن يشتمل على معاني الكتب المتقدمة فتاليها تالي الكتب القيمة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the Quran contains several kinds of knowledge, each kind being a book; al-Suddi says its rulings are just.
rows.anchor: معناه في القرآن كتب قيمة بمعنى أنه يشتمل على أنواع من العلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book differed about Muhammad only after he came, despite prophecy of him in their scriptures and by their messengers; some then believed and others disbelieved.
rows.anchor: وما اختلف هؤلاء في أمر محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم إلا من بعد ما جاءتهم البشارة به في كتبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were commanded only to worship God alone, a principle no revealed religion changes, sincerely without mixing in worship of another, and to establish prayer and pay required alms.
rows.anchor: لم يأمرهم الله تعالى إلا لأن يعبدوا الله وحده لا يشركون بعبادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hanif means turning from all religions to Islam and believing in all messengers. Atiyya and Ibn Abbas say with Muslim it means pilgrim, but alone it means Muslim; Ibn Jubayr says Arabs use it for one who performs pilgrimage and circumcision; Qatada describes circumcision, prohibitions on incest, and pilgrimage rites.
rows.anchor: مائلين عن جميع الأديان إلى دين الإسلام مسلمين مؤمنين بالرسل كلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'That' refers to the religion just described; alternatively, it means the religion or law of the upright. Al-Nadr asked al-Khalil, who explained qayyima as a plural related to those who stand for monotheism.
rows.anchor: أي دين الكتب القيمة التي تقدم ذكرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse rebuts determinism because it plainly says people were created to worship God; it also supports requiring intention for ritual purity, since worship and sincere devotion require intention.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دلالة على بطلان مذهب أهل الجبر لأن فيها تصريحا بأنه سبحانه إنما خلق الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unbelievers among the People of the Book and polytheists deny God's unity and His Prophet's message or associate another deity in worship; they remain in Hell and are the worst creatures.
rows.anchor: يعني من جحد توحيد الله وأنكر نبوة نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم ومن أشرك معه إلها آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who believe and do good are the best of creation.
rows.anchor: الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات أولئك هم خير البرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their reward is eternal Eden gardens with rivers; God is pleased with their obedience and they with the reward, or He is pleased with their monotheism, purity, and obedience and they with His mercy and favor.
rows.anchor: رضي الله عنهم إذ وحدوه ونزهوه عما لا يليق به وأطاعوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'That' means God's satisfaction and their reward, granted to whoever fears his Lord, avoids sins, and obeys Him.
rows.anchor: الرضا والثواب { لمن خشي ربه } فترك معاصيه وفعل طاعاته

rows.speaker: علي عن يزيد بن شراحيل الأنصاري
rows.claim: In a report to Ali's secretary, the Prophet interprets 'best creation' as Ali's Shi'a, promising to meet them at the Pool as bright, marked people when nations assemble for judgment.
rows.anchor: إلى يزيد بن شراحيل الأنصاري كاتب علي ع قال سمعت عليا ع يقول قبض رسول الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن الضحاك عن مقاتل
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse 'they are the best creation' was revealed about Ali and his household.
rows.anchor: نزلت في علي ع وأهل بيته

rows.speaker: الكسائي وأبان عن عاصم وعلي
rows.claim: Some transmissions from al-Kisa'i and Aban from Asim, and Ali's reading, put damma on the y in both 'he is shown good' and 'he is shown evil'.
rows.anchor: بضم الياء فيهما وهي رواية أبان عن عاصم أيضا

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وروح ورويس
rows.claim: Most readers use fatha on y; Abu Jaafar, Ruh, and Ruways instead use a lightly shortened damma on the h in both places.
rows.anchor: والباقون يره بفتح الياء في الموضعين إلا أن أبا جعفر وروحا ورويسا قرؤوا

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: With fatha, the verb is seen with the eye; with damma it is passive from the causative 'show', meaning its recompense is shown. A connecting waw after the pronoun is preferred, as in ordinary words and a poetic example.
rows.anchor: من قرأ يره جعل الفعل منقولا من رأيت زيدا إذا أدركته ببصرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zalzala is intense shaking; zilzal with kasra is the verbal noun and with fatha is the name, synonymous with shaking and quaking.
rows.anchor: الزلزلة شدة الاضطراب والزلزال بكسر الزاي المصدر وبفتحها الاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth's burdens means its dead, compared with a weight carried in the womb; Arabic also calls a mighty chief a burden upon the earth, whose death removes that weight.
rows.anchor: والأثقال جمع الثقل وسمى سبحانه الموتى أثقالا تشبيها بالحمل الذي يكون في البطن

rows.speaker: الخنساء
rows.claim: Al-Khansa's elegy for Sakhr says the earth relieved its burden by his death, meaning its chief and glory were lost.
rows.anchor:
أبعد ابن عمرو من آل الشريد
حلت به الأرض أثقالها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternate interpretation says the earth adorns its dead with ornaments.
rows.anchor: معناه زينت موتاها به من الحلية

rows.speaker: الشمردل اليربوعي
rows.claim: Al-Shamardal's elegy describes the earth's burdens settling with his brother in his resting place.
rows.anchor: وحلت به أثقالها الأرض وانتهى

rows.speaker: زهير بن أبي سلمى والنابغة الذبياني وكعب بن زهير
rows.claim: A story says Zuhayr got stuck on a line about becoming light or heavy in the earth; al-Nabigha could not complete it, but the young Ka'b supplied the ending and impressed his father.
rows.anchor: وذكر ابن السائب أن زهير بن أبي سلمى قال بيتا ثم أكدى فمر به النابغة الذبياني

rows.speaker: العجاج
rows.claim: Al-Ajjaj uses wahi and waha interchangeably in a line about a decision settling, showing that the two forms are synonymous.
rows.anchor: وأوحى ووحى بمعنى واحد قال العجاج:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the syntax, the word idha is governed by 'whoever does'; khayran is an accusative specification. An alternative makes 'the earth reports' govern it, or treats 'what is wrong with it' as repeated at that day before the answer that God inspired it; tuhaddith can address the hearer or describe the earth.
rows.anchor: وقوله { خيرا } منصوب على التمييز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth will be shaken violently for the Resurrection; the possessive stresses a world-wide quake unlike ordinary local earthquakes, underscoring its severity.
rows.anchor: إذا حركت الأرض تحريكا شديدا لقيام الساعة زلزالها الذي كتب عليها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والجبائي
rows.claim: The earth ejects its buried dead alive for recompense.
rows.anchor: أي أخرجت موتاها المدفونة فيها تخرجها أحياء للجزاء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, it casts out hidden treasures and minerals for people to see, making sinners regret having disobeyed God for them and then left them useless; those treasures also brand their foreheads, sides, and backs.
rows.anchor: معناه لفظت ما فيها من كنوزها ومعادنها فتلقيها على ظهرها ليراها أهل الموقف

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: The person asks in astonishment what has happened to the shaking earth.
rows.anchor: ويقول الإنسان متعجبا ما للأرض تتزلزل يعني ما لها حدث فيها ما لم يعرف منها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the human is an unbeliever denying resurrection who asks what shook the earth and brought it to this condition.
rows.anchor: إن المراد بالإنسان الكافر لأن المؤمن معترف بها لا يسأل عنها

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet explains that the earth reports the deeds each servant performed on it, naming the acts and their days.
rows.anchor: أخبارها أن تشهد على كل عبد وأنه بما عمل على ظهرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth may testify by being made an animal capable of speech, or by displaying something that stands in for speech; this is like saying tearful eyes testify to sleeplessness or the poet's eyes obey.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يقلبها حيوانا يقدر على النطق ويجوز أن يظهر فيها ما يقوم مقام الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God inspired the earth by teaching it to report its news; alternatively, He secretly conveyed instructions to it so it could cast out its treasures and dead.
rows.anchor: أي ألهمها عرفها بأن تحدث أخبارها

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says the earth speaks at God's inspiration and permission.
rows.anchor: تحدث أخبارها بوحي الله وأذنه لها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says God gave the earth permission to report what people did upon it.
rows.anchor: أذن لها لتخبر بما عمل عليها

rows.speaker: ربيعة الحرشي عن النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet urges keeping ablution and prayer, and treating the earth well: it is one's mother, and reports every good or evil act done upon it.
rows.anchor: حافظوا على الوضوء وخير أعمالكم الصلاة وتحفظوا من الأرض

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري عن النبي
rows.claim: Abu Said says to raise the call to prayer in open country because every jinn, human, and stone that hears it will testify for the caller.
rows.anchor: لا يسمعه جن ولا إنس ولا حجر إلا يشهد له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the presentation at the Judgment, people leave in separate groups, believers apart and each religious community apart, for their destinations; this is like the verses that say they will separate.
rows.anchor: أي يرجع الناس عن موقف الحساب بعد العرض متفرقين أهل الإيمان على حدة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: To see their deeds means to see their recompense; people return in groups to their destinations in Paradise or Hell.
rows.anchor: ليروا جزاء أعمالهم عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the seeing means inward knowledge of one's deeds at that moment or literally seeing their records, which omit nothing small or great.
rows.anchor: معنى الرؤية هنا المعرفة بالأعمال عند تلك الحال وهي رؤية القلب
